terms.definition: A type that groups related values together, and every copy you make is independent of the others.
terms.example: I made the user profile a struct, so changing a copy does not touch the original.

terms.definition: A type that groups data and actions together, and it can inherit from a parent type.
terms.example: The view controller is a class, because UIKit needs it to inherit from UIViewController.

terms.definition: A type where many variables point to the same single instance, so a change through one variable shows up in all of them.
terms.example: Because it is a reference type, both screens see the update as soon as one of them changes it.

dialogue.title: Why do two screens show different data?
dialogue.setting: Slack huddle about a strange bug

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, I have a strange bug. The settings screen changes the theme, but the home screen does not update.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do you pass the settings to the home screen?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is a struct. I pass it in the initializer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That is the reason. Every copy of a struct is independent.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the home screen has its own copy, and the change never reaches it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. That is the good side of a struct too. A change to a copy never hurts the original.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then should I make the settings a class?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Maybe. A class is a reference type, so both screens point to the same instance.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And a change on one screen shows up on the other.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. A class can also inherit from a parent, like UIViewController.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I changed it to a class, and now it works. Should I make every model a class?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, please. Prefer a struct for simple data, like a user profile.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why? A class feels more powerful.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Because a reference type can be changed from anywhere. That makes bugs hard to find.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm. I disagree a little. For shared settings, I want one place that everyone sees.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fair. For shared state, a reference type is the right tool. For a plain value, use a struct.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay. The settings stay a class, and the profile stays a struct.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Perfect. A struct, a class, and a reference type. Choose on purpose.
I made the profile a struct, so a copy is independent.
